git_commit_note: Points at the per-language RRF reweight commit (RRF_LANGUAGE_WEIGHTS, _rrf_weights_for_medium, weighted reciprocal_rank_fusion). Committed as the NEXT commit after this code, pushed immediately, same convention as Phase 1/2. This is a MITIGATION on top of a disclosed limitation (pervasive Tamil OCR corruption, ~88% of a manually-inspected sample -- see the diagnosis pass preceding this commit), NOT a fix for that limitation. The corrupted text itself is unchanged; this only reweights fusion toward BM25 for Tamil-medium queries (sparse_w=3.0 vs dense_w=1.0, tuned empirically against Tamil-only pre-rerank R@5 on a 25-item sample) so hybrid retrieval stops being dragged down by dense embeddings computed over corrupted text. English weighting is untouched (1:1) -- dense-only was already healthy there.
method: Same gold set and stages as phase2_retrieval_results.json (BM25-only / hybrid pre-rerank / hybrid post-rerank via rerank_with_trust / cross_corpus_fusion pre+post-rerank), re-run unchanged EXCEPT for the Tamil-medium RRF weight change described above. bm25_only and cross_corpus_fusion_* numbers are expected (and confirmed) bit-identical to Phase 2, since neither path calls reciprocal_rank_fusion with per-language weights -- BM25-only never calls it at all, and cross_corpus_fusion merges the two corpora pools directly rather than via single-corpus RRF. The English hybrid numbers are also expected (and confirmed) bit-identical, since English weighting (1.0/1.0) is unchanged. The only intended-to-move numbers are the single-corpus "tamil" bucket and the Tamil leg of bilingual/tanglish single-corpus buckets (bilingual_vs_TA, tanglish_vs_TA), where medium="tamil" now triggers the 3x BM25 weight.

comparison_vs_phase2.english_pre_and_post_rerank: bit-identical to Phase 2, as expected (weighting unchanged)
comparison_vs_phase2.cross_corpus_fusion_bilingual_and_tangli: bit-identical to Phase 2, as expected (fusion path does not use per-language RRF)

tanglish_vs_TA_post_rerank_recall_3.note: One item (n=9 bucket) that was recovered within top-3 after rerank in Phase 2 is not recovered in Phase 2b. This bucket is raw (non-transliterated) Romanized Tanglish text matched directly against the Tamil-script corpus via single-corpus retrieval -- both Phase 2 and Phase 2b scores here are near-zero across the board (this bucket was never the point; the meaningful Tanglish path is tanglish_fused, which goes through transliteration and is unaffected). Disclosed per the "confirm no regression" instruction, but not considered a real regression given n=9, near-zero baseline on both sides, and that this bucket is not the one the reweight targeted or claims to help.

comparison_vs_phase2.bilingual_vs_TA: recall values unchanged or improved (recall_10 pre: 0.1429->0.1429, post: 0.1429->0.2143); small MRR wobble in both directions on this n=14 bucket, not a material regression.
